You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like December 2022 or January 2023. Fed funds at 4.33% points to December 2022, when the effective rate was about 4.33% after the mid-December hike to a 4.25–4.50% target range. In January 2023 the effective rate was about 4.33% as well, because the rate was unchanged until the February meeting.

Other readings fit January 2023 better:
- The unemployment rate of 3.5% fits both December 2022 and January 2023 (January 2023 was 3.4%, though that figure was released in February).
- Headline CPI of 6.42% is the figure for December 2022 (6.5%) or November 2022 (7.1%), while core CPI of 5.69% fits neither cleanly. December 2022 headline was 6.5% and core 5.7%, so these are close to December's published values.
- The three-month change in the fed funds rate is +1.25. From September 2022 (about 3.08%) to December 2022 (4.33%) that is +1.25, which matches December. From October 2022 (3.08%) to January 2023 (4.33%) it would also be +1.25.
- Equity 1m return of +6.0% and 3m of +5.0% fits January 2023 (S&P +6.3%) better than December 2022 (-5.8%), so the month is January 2023.
- Emerging-market equity 3m of +22.5% and developed ex-US 3m of +20% fit January 2023, following the strong rally from October 2022.
- The 10-year yield of 3.55% fits January 2023, which ended near 3.5%. December 2022 ended near 3.88%.
- Payrolls averaging +247K over three months fits the data available at the end of January 2023, which includes the January report released in early February, and the CPI figure is the December reading.

The tension is CPI at 6.42%, which is somewhat off the published 6.5%, but the market figures settle it.
